summary: Internal refactor: each sketch relation kind compiles its own solver equations from its definition, and the solver receives exactly the equations it did before. The pure equation model and the compiler move from the worker code to the domain, in src/domain/cad/sketch-solver/, and the encoding for the native module stays with the worker. A lowering context hides where each parameter sits: a relation asks for a point's parameters by id, an edge's support, centre or size by what the edge gives, and a driving value by its scalar key through the relation's definition. It refuses an operand that cannot give what is asked with a typed error, and tags each equation with the relation that emitted it. It lowers each relation, and each arc's own equation, whole or not at all: if a lowering throws partway, the context drops the equations and radial holds it emitted and gives back its tags before passing the error on. The compiler already stopped at the first refusal, so nothing partial ever reached the solver. Within the context only its capability tables name line, arc and circle; the compiler still gives each circle a radius parameter, and a fillet still refuses a corner without its arc, as before. Each of the 25 definitions gains lower, which emits the kind's equations through the context, check, which runs the kind's existing graph check, and an agent meaning, the text the constraint inspection showed for it. The compiler is now a loop that sends each relation to its definition; its switch over 21 relation cases is removed, and so are the graph checks' chain of kind tests and the inspection's meaning table. The tangent, angle and symmetry branch logic and the fillet, chamfer and pattern ownership stay with their kinds. Each driving value declares the quantity it measures, length, angle, count or ratio, which only a test reads in this release. The solver's retry from off a circle's centre now reads the radial holds the compiler records, instead of looking for point-on-curve relations.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files, agents or controller output. Sketches parse, solve, draw and save exactly as before: for every graph of the relation baseline, every input of the frozen solver corpus and every input the solver benchmarks solve, the compiled equations keep their kinds, order, operands, values, tags, sources and fixed parameters, the native module answers them the same way, and the graph checks, the constraint inspection rows and the solver's own attempt are unchanged, errors included. The worker protocol version stays 7.

checklist.schema: No CAD, sketch graph, UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. The native protocol stays version 7, with the same buffers. The Rust solver and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version, cancellation or WebMCP behaviour change. Sending a relation to its definition indexes the frozen definition table by kind, as the switch did, and the graph checks run where and as often as before, each with one lookup per relation in place of a chain of kind tests. The lowering context is made once per compile, as the compiler's own helpers were, and passes edges as each relation resolved them, so it builds no index of the sketch unless a relation holds only ids. Lowering each relation whole or not at all keeps two counts and a tag to restore if it throws, which costs nothing measurable. Nothing new runs on pointer moves, hover or drags.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added, removed or changed. The constraint inspection reads each relation's meaning from its definition, with the same text, and its driving values from the definition's scalar keys, with the same rows. The quantity each driving value declares is not shown or exposed, and no agent-visible text changes. No UI control is added.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. The repository gains a test fixture of the equations compiled before this change, which is not part of the built app.
checklist.verification: Equation baseline: a new fixture records, at 4afad29c (0.0.787), every input of three groups: the 2,844 relation-baseline graphs placed at seeded coordinates with seeded parameters, the 1,774 inputs of the frozen solver corpus over its 1,215 graphs, and the 513 distinct inputs the solver benchmarks solve over 162 graphs. For each it holds the compiled model in full or the compile error, the native answer, and hashes of the graph checks, the constraint inspection rows and the solver attempt; the manifest gives inputs, normalization and regeneration, and recording again from a fresh snapshot gave the committed bytes both from the stored benchmark inputs and from a new capture. All 5,131 inputs are identical: 5,111 compile to 122,709 equations, 2,700 of them drag targets, over 91,451 relations, and 20 refuse with the same three errors. Tests touched: import paths only in cadSketchNativeRuntime, cadSketchNativeDefinition, cadSketchNativeSolver, nativeBaseline and planeGcsCorpus tests and helpers, and the native A/B benchmark script. New: the equation baseline test, and cadSketchLowering (refusals for each capability and unknown operands, nothing emitted on refusal, a relation refused partway through leaving none of its equations, radial holds or tags behind, which fails without the rollback, every scalar key declares a quantity). Test fix: the cad-sketch-constraints line definition colour test read the hover colour right after moving the mouse, before the hover was drawn; it now polls until the stroke leaves the unhovered colour, then reads it. That race existed before this change, and the test's assertions are unchanged. Mutations, each caught by the baseline: Coincident emitting Y before X (847, 196 and 1 inputs differ; 4 tests in 2 files, no behaviour suite), a fixed point's Y reading position.0 (14 tests in 9 files), offset swapping its points (16 tests in 8 files). Performance, alternating a 4afad29c snapshot and this branch on one host: compiling all 5,131 inputs, median of each process's fastest round 53.25 ms before and 53.39 ms after over 10 processes per side; the 454 drag and sweep inputs 10.87 and 10.97 ms; the graph checks 116.78 and 107.64 ms. A first version that looked edges up by id cost about 0.6 µs per compile and was changed. The whole-or-nothing lowering was measured with the compiler before and after it running in one process, alternating every round, 20 rounds per side in 8 processes: the median fastest round was 50.14 and 50.26 ms for all 5,131 inputs, a median per-process difference of +0.28% (from -0.61% to +1.17%), with every input compiling the same. The solver-workloads benchmark (workloads, edits, drag, sweep), 7 runs per side, overlaps on every stage: workloads parse and compile 6.0 and 6.2 ms, native call 30.4 and 28.2 ms, validation 6.5 and 5.7 ms in sums of p50s; drag frames parse and compile 316 [281 to 340] and 333 [265 to 365] ms, native call 2,189 and 2,108 ms, validation 331 and 313 ms; no correctness failure. Checks: full Vitest 6,738 of 6,738 in 573 files (there is no native-differential project; the projects are pure-domain and browser); CadSketchCanvasRender 18 of 18, unchanged; npm run build including the e2e type-check and the documentation check; oxlint with zero findings; npm run ui:check; check-release, and against origin/main at 4afad29c. Chromium specs, each run alone with two workers: on the final build, cad-sketch-constraints 28 of 28 at the first run, and its line definition colour test 5 of 5 repeats; on the build before the whole-or-nothing lowering and the test fix, cad-sketch-relation-glyphs 7, cad-sketch-dimension-selection 4, cad-sketch-selectable-axes 1.
